name: Autonomous Shell Portability Healer
description: Implements autonomous regression test healing for shell portability issues, enabling FADE to fix BSD/GNU compatibility problems overnight without human intervention.

context.problem: FADE sessions fail overnight when regression tests hit shell portability issues (BSD vs GNU coreutils). Developer wakes up to blocked session with zero progress from 3am-7am.
context.realWorldIncident: LiveCalc PRD-LC-013 failed at 03:05 with 'head: illegal line count' error. Lost 5.3 hours of potential productivity waiting for manual intervention.
context.impact: Overnight runs blocked by trivial shell syntax issues that have known, safe fixes. Hours wasted on problems that could be auto-resolved in seconds.

solution: Add autonomous healing layer that detects shell portability errors in test output, applies known safe fixes from a whitelist, retries tests, and continues the session if successful. All healing events logged for audit.

userStories.title: Detect shell portability errors in test output
userStories.description: As FADE, I want to detect when regression tests fail due to shell portability issues so I can distinguish fixable errors from real failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture test output to temporary file when tests fail
Pattern match against known portability error signatures
Detect 'head: illegal line count' errors
Detect 'tail: illegal offset' errors
Detect 'sed: -i needs an argument' errors
Return match info: error type, affected file, line number if available
Detection completes in < 2 seconds

userStories.title: Apply known fixes from portability whitelist
userStories.description: As FADE, I want to apply proven safe fixes from a whitelist so I can heal tests autonomously without risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Maintain whitelist of known-safe fix patterns in fade/standards/shell-portability-fixes.sh
Fix pattern: 'head -n -X' → 'sed "${X}d"' (remove last X lines)
Fix pattern: 'head -n-X' → 'sed "${X}d"'
Fix pattern: 'tail -n +X' → 'tail -n +X' (already portable, but validate)
Fix pattern: 'sed -i' → 'sed -i.bak' (add backup extension)
Apply fixes only to files in fade/tests/ directory
Create backup of original file before applying fix
Log each fix application to healing-log.md with timestamp, file, pattern, replacement

userStories.title: Retry tests after healing and continue if successful
userStories.description: As FADE, I want to retry tests after applying fixes and continue the session if they pass, so overnight runs don't block on fixable issues.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-run regression tests after applying fixes
If tests pass: commit fixes with message 'chore: auto-heal shell portability (FEAT-012)'
If tests pass: append success entry to healing-log.md with time saved estimate
If tests pass: continue to next user story in current PRD
If tests fail again: attempt up to 3 total healing cycles
If tests still fail after 3 attempts: exit gracefully with detailed failure log
Maximum 5 minutes total for all healing attempts
Display healing summary: 'Auto-healed shell portability issue in 47s. Session continuing.'

userStories.title: Maintain healing audit log
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want all healing events logged so I can review what was fixed overnight and verify safety.
acceptanceCriteria: Create/append to fade/healing-log.md
Log format: '## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM - [SEVERITY] PRD-ID/US-ID'
Log includes: detected error pattern, affected files, fix applied, test result, time to heal
Log includes: estimated time saved (assume 5.3 hours for overnight blocks)
Log includes: git commit hash if fix was committed
healing-log.md is append-only, never auto-deleted
Log entry created even if healing fails (for debugging)

userStories.title: Safety constraints enforcement
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want strict safety constraints so autonomous healing can't damage production code.
acceptanceCriteria: Healing only applies to files matching 'fade/tests/**/*'
Healing explicitly blocks patterns: 'src/', 'lib/', 'bin/', any file without 'test' in path
Healing only applies patterns from approved whitelist (no dynamic pattern generation)
Each fix creates .bak backup before modification
If file path doesn't match allowed patterns, log error and skip healing
Integration test: Attempt to heal file in src/ directory, verify it's blocked

userStories.title: Document portability patterns in standards
userStories.description: As a developer, I want shell portability patterns documented so I can write portable tests from the start.
acceptanceCriteria: Create/update fade/standards/shell-portability.md
Document 'head -n -X' issue and sed alternative
Document 'sed -i' differences between BSD/GNU
Document portable alternatives for common operations
Include examples of correct usage
Link from architecture.md in standards reference table

technicalNotes.architecture: Add healing layer in fade/lib/auto-healer.sh, called from run.sh after test failures
technicalNotes.errorDetection: Grep patterns against test output captured to /tmp/fade-test-output-$$.log
technicalNotes.fixWhitelist: Stored in fade/standards/shell-portability-fixes.sh as associative arrays
technicalNotes.safetyModel: Whitelist-only fixes + directory restrictions + backup files
technicalNotes.timeout: 5 minute maximum for all healing attempts, 15 second timeout per fix application
technicalNotes.noAgentFramework: Does not require specialized agent framework, uses inline bash logic

filesToModify.changes: Add healing hook after regression test failures. Capture test output, call auto-healer, retry if healed.
Add autonomous healing section, document safety constraints and audit logging.

mustHave: Detect shell portability errors with >95% accuracy
Retry tests and continue session if healed
Safety constraints prevent production code modification
Integration test: Simulate PRD-LC-013 failure, verify auto-heal in <2 minutes
niceToHave: Healing success rate metrics in session summary
Notification when healing occurs (console only for Phase 1)
Expandable pattern library for future portability issues

risks.risk: Auto-healing applies wrong fix, breaks tests further
risks.mitigation: Whitelist-only fixes with proven patterns. 3-attempt limit. Backup files. Safety constraints on directory access.
Only heals shell syntax errors, not test logic failures. Detailed audit log. User reviews healing-log.md regularly.

definitionOfDone: All 6 user stories have passing acceptance criteria
Integration test simulates overnight failure and verifies auto-heal
healing-log.md correctly logs all healing events
Safety constraints verified: cannot modify files outside fade/tests/
Documentation updated in architecture.md and shell-portability.md
No false-positive heals in test suite (zero test intent changes)
